newsitem.title: UKRAINE: U.S. seeks explanation of Belarus "plot" charge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks explanation of Belarus "plot" charge.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it was seeking an explanation of charges by Belarussian president Lukashenko that western embassies were trying to destabilise his country.
A statement from the U.S. embassy in Minsk, faxed to Reuters in the Ukrainian capital Kiev, described Lukashenko's charges as outrageous.
It said the embassy had asked the Belarussian foreign ministry to explain Lukashenko's comments, which apparently reacted to discussions at a closed-door meeting of NATO ambassadors on September 11.

Lukashenko, appearing on television on Sunday night, accused the diplomats of seeking to impede his attempts to get his new constitution accepted during a referendum he plans for November, Russia's Interfax news agency said.
He said the United States planned to send a commission to write a report on human rights in the former Soviet republic.
But he said Belarus remained under control, despite attempts to destabilise the situation. "The nation will support its president," he said.
The U.S. statement said the embassy had reported the comments to Washington. "We consider these statements and the activities they imply outrageous," it said.

Lukashenko said the U.S. ambassador and a British diplomat had suggested that cash rewards be given to Belarus politicians who impede Lukashenko's initiatives. He said the diplomats planned to use their countries' money to finance a trip for opposition journalists to London and Washington.
Opposition parliamentarians have accused Lukashenko of dragging Belarus towards a Nazi-style dictatorship and some have suggested introducing a constitution which abolishes the post of president.
In April Lukashenko threatened to expel diplomats who attended mass rallies denouncing his pro-Russian policies and withdraw accreditations from journalists who covered them.
The United States in August granted political asylum to two opposition leaders after they fled the country.
